title: World powers of Bible history
intro: The powers that ruled over God’s people, one after another, with the events where each one enters the Bible record.

items.name: Egypt
items.text: The first world power of Bible history. A Pharaoh who did not know Joseph enslaved Israel. Egypt’s power was shaken at the Exodus, when Jehovah brought ten plagues and destroyed its army in the Red Sea.
items.sources: si Study 3, chart of dates; it “Egypt, Egyptian”
items.approx: The chart dates Egypt’s rise to “after 1600 B.C.E.” No end date is given. The bar stops at the Exodus, and Egypt’s later contacts with Israel are shown as events.

pictures.title: The Miracle at the Red Sea

items.name: Assyria
items.text: Assyria pressed on Israel from the days of King Menahem, destroyed Samaria in 740 B.C.E. and invaded Judah in 732 B.C.E. Its capital, Nineveh, fell in 632 B.C.E.
items.sources: it “Assyria”; si Study 3, chart of dates
items.approx: The article gives no date for when Assyria became dominant. The bar starts at its first recorded move into Israel, in Menahem’s reign.

items.name: Babylon
items.text: After Nineveh fell, Babylon became the dominant power. Nebuchadnezzar defeated Egypt at Carchemish, took Jewish captives and destroyed Jerusalem in 607 B.C.E. In Daniel’s vision Babylon is the head of gold.
items.sources: nwt Appendix B9; si Study 3, chart of dates

pictures.title: A Kingdom That Will Last Forever

items.name: Medo-Persia
items.text: Cyrus conquered Babylon in one night and in 537 B.C.E. decreed that the Jews could return. Under Persian kings the temple and the walls of Jerusalem were rebuilt.
items.sources: nwt Appendix B9; si Study 3, chart of dates

items.name: Greece
items.text: Alexander the Great conquered Persia, and Greece ruled Judea from 332 B.C.E. After his death his empire was divided. The Greek Septuagint translation was begun about 280 B.C.E.
items.sources: nwt Appendix B9; si Study 3, chart of dates

items.name: Rome
items.text: Rome ruled over Israel from 63 B.C.E. Jesus was born, preached and was put to death under Roman rule, and Rome destroyed Jerusalem in 70 C.E. The chart then names Anglo-America, which came into being during World War I (1914-1918 C.E.), beyond the years shown here.
items.sources: nwt Appendix B9; si Study 3, chart of dates

items.name: Joseph sold into Egypt
items.text: Joseph’s brothers sell him and he is taken to Egypt as a slave.
items.sources: si Study 3, chart of dates

items.name: Joseph made ruler under Pharaoh
items.text: Joseph interprets Pharaoh’s dreams and is put in charge of Egypt’s food supply.
items.sources: si Study 3, chart of dates

items.name: Jacob’s family moves to Egypt
items.text: Jacob and his whole household come to live in Egypt.
items.sources: si Study 3, chart of dates

items.name: The Exodus
items.text: After the tenth plague Israel leaves Egypt, and Pharaoh’s army is destroyed in the Red Sea.
items.sources: si Study 3, chart of dates

pictures.title: The Miracle at the Red Sea

items.name: Shishak of Egypt invades Judah
items.text: In Rehoboam’s fifth year Shishak takes the treasures of the temple and the palace.
items.sources: si Study 3, chart of dates; it “Egypt, Egyptian”

items.name: Assyria takes Samaria
items.text: After a three-year siege Samaria falls and the ten-tribe kingdom of Israel is carried into exile.
items.sources: si Study 3, chart of dates

items.name: Sennacherib invades Judah
items.text: In Hezekiah’s fourteenth year the Assyrians take Judah’s fortified cities. An angel strikes down 185,000 of them.
items.sources: si Study 3, chart of dates; it “Assyria”

items.name: Nineveh falls
items.text: The Assyrian capital falls to the Chaldeans and the Medes.
items.sources: si Study 3, chart of dates

items.name: Pharaoh Necho defeats Josiah
items.text: Necho marches north and King Josiah is fatally wounded at Megiddo.
items.sources: it “Egypt, Egyptian”

items.name: Babylon defeats Egypt at Carchemish
items.text: Nebuchadnezzar decisively defeats Pharaoh Necho and becomes king of Babylon.
items.sources: si Study 3, chart of dates; it “Egypt, Egyptian”

items.name: First Jewish captives taken to Babylon
items.text: Nebuchadnezzar takes King Jehoiachin and many others, Daniel and Ezekiel among them, to Babylon.
items.sources: si Study 3, chart of dates

items.name: Babylon destroys Jerusalem
items.text: The temple is burned, the city destroyed and the land left desolate.
items.sources: si Study 3, chart of dates; nwt Appendix B9

items.name: Babylon falls to the Medes and Persians
items.text: Cyrus takes Babylon in one night.
items.sources: si Study 3, chart of dates; nwt Appendix B9

items.name: Cyrus lets the Jews return
items.text: The decree of Cyrus ends the seventy years of desolation.
items.sources: si Study 3, chart of dates; nwt Appendix B9

items.name: Second temple completed
items.text: Zerubbabel finishes rebuilding the temple.
items.sources: si Study 3, chart of dates

items.name: Decree to rebuild Jerusalem
items.text: In the twentieth year of Artaxerxes, Nehemiah rebuilds the walls. The seventy weeks begin.
items.sources: si Study 3, chart of dates

items.name: Alexander conquers Persia
items.text: Alexander the Great conquers Persia. Greece had begun to rule Judea in 332 B.C.E.
items.sources: nwt Appendix B9; si Study 3, chart of dates

items.name: Greek Septuagint begun
items.text: Translation of the Hebrew Scriptures into Greek begins.
items.sources: si Study 3, chart of dates

items.name: Temple rededicated
items.text: The temple is rededicated after being desecrated under Greek rule.
items.sources: si Study 3, chart of dates

items.name: Rome rules Jerusalem
items.text: Rome takes control of Jerusalem.
items.sources: si Study 3, chart of dates; nwt Appendix B9

items.name: Jesus put to death
items.text: Under the Roman governor Pontius Pilate, Jesus is put to death and on the third day is resurrected.
items.sources: si Study 3, chart of dates

items.name: Rome destroys Jerusalem
items.text: Jerusalem and its temple are destroyed by the Romans.
items.sources: si Study 3, chart of dates; nwt Appendix B9
